functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Deepest hypothenar muscle; cups the palm during opposition, the hand's structural mirror of opponens pollicis.
functional_compartments.source: Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity muscle architecture model (fascicle length, pennation, PCSA)

motor_endplate_zones.method: modified Sihler's stain intramuscular nerve mapping
motor_endplate_zones.notes: Major branches densely distributed in the middle and distal parts of the muscle belly. The source states this in words rather than as a measured percentage -- it is a hand-surgery paper, not an injection-targeting one -- so the range is that wording read as thirds of muscle length, and nothing narrower is claimed.
motor_endplate_zones.source: Xie P, Jiang Y, Zhang X, Yang S, 'The Study of Intramuscular Nerve Distribution Patterns and Relative Spindle Abundance of the Thenar and Hypothenar Muscles in Human Hand', PLoS One 7(12):e51538 (2012), doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0051538 -- 40 hands from 20 adult cadavers, modified Sihler's stain with haematoxylin-eosin spindle counts

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity muscle architecture model (fascicle length, pennation, PCSA)

relative_muscle_spindle_abundance.method: actual spindle count divided by the count predicted from muscle mass, by Banks' allometric correction
relative_muscle_spindle_abundance.notes: Extramuscular nerve trunk length 0.49 +/- 0.26 cm. Comparable across muscles of different size because it is normalised by predicted count rather than by mass.
relative_muscle_spindle_abundance.source: Xie P, Jiang Y, Zhang X, Yang S, 'The Study of Intramuscular Nerve Distribution Patterns and Relative Spindle Abundance of the Thenar and Hypothenar Muscles in Human Hand', PLoS One 7(12):e51538 (2012), doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0051538 -- 40 hands from 20 adult cadavers, modified Sihler's stain with haematoxylin-eosin spindle counts

notes: Highest spindle abundance of the hypothenar muscles. Has the SHORTEST extramuscular nerve trunk of the whole group at 0.49 +/- 0.26 cm, which together with its depth is why it is almost never used as a transfer donor -- and, for the same reasons, why it is hard to reach blind.

trigger_points.location_description: Deepest hypothenar muscle, palpated over the 5th metacarpal and 5th CMC joint.
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: No distinct published Travell & Simons figure for opponens digiti minimi; clinically its trigger points produce deep ache along the 5th metacarpal and the ulnar palm.
trigger_points.notes: Differentiate from 5th CMC fracture-subluxation ('reverse Bennett') and hamate pathology by palpation level and provocation.
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual, Vol. 1 -- as cited in this atlas's uploaded hand intrinsic muscle reference document (clinical analogy to the Ch. 40 hypothenar pattern; no separate opponens digiti minimi figure is published)

clinical.compiled_by: repository owner (physician); hand_intrinsic_muscles_reference_v1.html, compiled 03/09/2026. Source hierarchy used. (1) Peer-reviewed anatomical and biomechanical studies (bibliographic data and abstracts retrieved via PubMed/NCBI, 01–03/09/2026; DOIs linked in the reference list); (2) reference textbooks — Standring (Gray's Anatomy, 42nd ed., 2021), Kapandji (2007), Green's Operative Hand Surgery (8th ed., 2022), Brand & Hollister (1999); (3) Simons, Travell & Simons, The Trigger Point Manual Vol. 1, 2nd ed. (1999) and 3rd ed. (2019) for trigger-point (TrP) referral patterns; (4) StatPearls/NCBI Bookshelf for cross-checking. No item below relies on blogs or unattributed aggregators; where secondary TrP summaries were used to confirm Travell & Simons figures, they are graded accordingly in the verification table.
clinical.function_biomechanics: Draws the 5th metacarpal palmarly and rotates it toward the thumb at the 5th CMC (a saddle-like, mobile joint), deepening the transverse metacarpal arch — the "cup" that lets the palm mould around handles, balls and instruments; opposite pole of the arch to OP [1][26]. Its loss flattens the ulnar palm and weakens cylindrical grip more than any single number captures; it is routinely underestimated next to its thumb counterpart.
clinical.adjacent_structures: Relations · closed sacs: Deepest hypothenar muscle, on the 5th metacarpal and the mobile 5th CMC joint capsule; the ulnar bursa and D5 flexor sheath lie radial to it [1][34].

trigger_points.referred_pain: No distinct Travell & Simons figure; TrPs produce deep ache along MC5 and the ulnar palm with tool use (hammering, racquets, pull-ups) [24]. Differentiate from 5th CMC fracture-subluxation ("reverse Bennett") and hamate pathology by palpation level and provocation [35].
trigger_points.source: [24] Simons DG, Travell JG, Simons LS. Travell & Simons' Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction: The Trigger Point Manual, Vol. 1: Upper Half of Body. 2nd ed. Baltimore: Williams & Wilkins; 1999 — Ch. 39 (adductor & opponens pollicis), Ch. 40 (interossei, lumbricals, abductor digiti minimi; pp. 786-793).; [35] Wolfe SW, Pederson WC, Kozin SH, Cohen MS (eds). Green's Operative Hand Surgery. 8th ed. Elsevier; 2022 — intrinsic muscle disorders, compartment syndrome, nerve palsy chapters.

pain_referred_into_this_muscle_from: As for the ulnar-hand list under ADM; deep palm spillover also from FCU and palmaris longus patterns [24][35].
clinical.caveat: Most myofascial hand pain is imported: shoulder-girdle, arm and forearm TrPs project distally far more often than intrinsic TrPs project proximally. Patterns below are the prototype maps of Simons, Travell & Simons (Vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1999; 3rd ed., 2019) — screening guides, not fingerprints; individual spread is wide [24][25]. Non-myofascial mimics are listed per zone for the same working position [5][29][31][35]. TrP → = habitual referred-pain direction of that muscle's trigger points (Simons, Travell & Simons 1999/2019); patterns are prototypes — individual variation is wide.
